summary: The published summary reads its machines again only when a claim can change them, not on every commit: a runtime observation reduces that runtime alone, and the machines are read again only when the set of hosts running runtimes changes

replay.detail: No claim is added or changed, and every claim replays unchanged. The change is to when an in-memory published view rereads its machines.

schema.detail: No tables, indexes, triggers, schema-version changes or data rewrites. The new read uses the existing runtime-subject index, two seeks per claim since the machines were read, and reduces at most 64 changed runtimes through the existing status reduction.

rules.detail: No checkpoint, retention, authority, admission or rules-version change.

compatibility.detail: The summary collection's rows and contract are unchanged. A peer's replication reachability, which changes with no claim, now reaches the machine counts at the 30-second clock period, as it already did on an idle daemon, instead of with the next unrelated commit.

downtime.detail: No startup work or interruption. The machines are held in memory and read again on the first refresh after a start.

manual.detail: No operator actions or configuration changes. ST3_ATTENTION_LIST=off still keeps per-window reads, which always read machines afresh.

recovery.detail: No persistent state. Rolling back reads the machines on every summary refresh again.
